subject: microbiology
title: Chemical Disinfectants: Glutaraldehyde, Formaldehyde, Phenolics and Efficacy Controls

steps.tx: **Glutaraldehyde** (2 percent alkaline activated) crosslinks microbial proteins into high level disinfection of endoscopes and heat sensitive instruments in 20 to 45 minutes and chemical sterilisation only after about ten hours immersion, billing staff asthma, dermatitis and colitis from inadequately rinsed scopes. Ortho phthalaldehyde (OPA) succeeded it in many units with faster cycles, no activation and its own staining and anaphylaxis footnotes.
steps.say: Glutaraldehyde disinfects in minutes and sterilises in ten hours; rinsing decides its colitis.

left.title: Glutaraldehyde profile
points: 2 percent alkaline, activation shelf life about 14 days

steps.tx: **Glutaraldehyde** at 2 percent, activated to alkaline pH, crosslinks microbial proteins. Immersion for 20 to 45 minutes gives high level disinfection of endoscopes and other heat sensitive instruments. Chemical sterilisation needs about ten hours in the same bath. Staff can develop asthma and dermatitis from the vapour, and patients can develop colitis if a scope is rinsed poorly. Ortho phthalaldehyde replaced it in many units because cycles are faster and activation is unnecessary, but it stains skin and has its own anaphylaxis risk.
steps.say: Alkaline 2 percent glutaraldehyde crosslinks proteins. Endoscopes are disinfected in 20 to 45 minutes, but sterilisation takes about ten hours. Vapour can cause staff asthma and dermatitis. A poorly rinsed scope can cause colitis. Ortho phthalaldehyde is faster and needs no activation, yet it stains and can trigger anaphylaxis.

vis.alt: An endoscope soaks in activated glutaraldehyde while a minimum effective concentration test strip is held beside the bath.
vis.caption: A heat sensitive endoscope is immersed in alkaline glutaraldehyde, and a test strip checks that the bath is still above its minimum effective concentration. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Formaldehyde** preserves anatomy and historically sterilised by gas (formalin tablets in sealed cabinets for blankets and catheters), disinfects by fumigation now largely retired for carcinogenicity and irritation, and survives daily as formalin tissue fixation and vaccine toxoid production (diphtheria and tetanus toxoids are formaldehyde's medical monuments). Its examination role is mostly recognising where it persists and why rooms stopped being fumigated.
steps.say: Formaldehyde left the fumigation room and stayed in the toxoid vial and specimen pot.

steps.tx: Phenolics carry disinfection's oldest chemistry: Lister's carbolic acid became cresols and Lysol floor and surface traditions, chloroxylenol (Dettol) skin antisepsis, and hexachlorophene cautionary tales (infant neurotoxicity ended its nursery career). The **phenol coefficient** (Rideal Walker, next lesson) was invented to grade this family against a Salmonella Typhi standard.
steps.say: Phenolics began with Lister's spray and were graded by comparison with phenol itself.

left.title: Phenolic family
points: Cresol and Lysol: surfaces and floors
Triclosan: retired from consumer soaps widely

right.title: Phenolic limits
points: Poor sporicidal and variable virucidal activity
Inactivated variably by organic matter (family dependent)

steps.tx: The **Spaulding classification** allocates every chemical by device risk (critical, semicritical, noncritical from the pasteurisation lesson), and disinfectant labels encode spectrum honestly: bactericidal, tuberculocidal, virucidal (enveloped easier than naked), fungicidal and sporicidal claims require separate standardised tests. A low level quaternary ammonium wipe cannot inherit glutaraldehyde's claims by proximity on the shelf.
steps.say: Read the label's claimed spectrum against the device's Spaulding class; shelves do not transfer claims.

left.title: Chemical classes by level
points: Sterilants and high level: glutaraldehyde, OPA, peracetic, peroxide
Antiseptics: the same chemistry on living tissue rules

steps.tx: **Alcohols (70 percent** ethyl or isopropyl) disinfect skin and small surfaces by protein denaturation needing water (absolute alcohol disinfects worse), evaporate before spore or naked virus claims, and anchor hand rubs whose C difficile spore failure this module repeats deliberately; chlorhexidine and iodophors extend skin antisepsis with residual activity and thyroid and neonatal cautions respectively.
steps.say: Seventy percent beats absolute because water helps denature; spores ignore alcohol entirely.

left.title: Alcohol facts
points: No sporicidal, weak on naked viruses
Hand rubs: technique and volume decide

right.title: Skin antiseptic partners
points: Chlorhexidine: residual activity, eye and ear cautions
Povidone iodine: broad, slower, thyroid cautions
Antiseptic versus disinfectant: tissue decides the word

steps.tx: A dilution chart sets **sodium hypochlorite** at a higher parts per million for a blood spill than for an ordinary surface, because blood consumes free chlorine. The stronger spill mix is not a skin antiseptic. Contact time has to be long enough for the available chlorine to act, and the working solution is made up fresh because stored bleach loses strength. Household stock is measured, not poured neat onto metal or skin.

vis.alt: Chlorine dilution chart in parts per million for blood spills and for surfaces
vis.caption: Sodium hypochlorite dilutions are listed in parts per million, higher for a blood spill than for a clean surface. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Hypochlorite is the** ward's adjustable sporicide: 1000 ppm available chlorine for surfaces, 5000 to 10000 ppm for blood spills and C difficile rooms, freshly diluted (light and age decay it), corrosive and inactivated by organic load so cleaning precedes it. Chlorine dioxide and superoxidised water occupy neighbouring niches with the same clean first commandment.
steps.say: Chlorine kills spores at spill strength and dies in dirt; clean first, dilute fresh.

steps.tx: **Chemical sterilant discipline** is measured in test strips and logs: minimum effective concentration strips each shift for glutaraldehyde and OPA, solution expiry by days and reuse counts, contact times timed (not estimated), and rinse water quality for final scope rinses. Most chemical disinfection failures in audits are concentration and contact failures, invisible until the strip or the outbreak reports them.
steps.say: If the strip was not dipped and the timer not set, the disinfection is a rumour.

left.title: Daily controls
points: Solution change dates and use counts
Timed immersion, full submersion, channels perfused

right.title: Failure patterns
points: Diluted below MEC by topping up

steps.tx: **Disinfectant selection in** an outbreak is spectrum escalation under supervision: norovirus and C difficile demand hypochlorite class agents regardless of routine contracts, Candida auris demands listed sporicidal and fungicidal products with contact discipline, and hand hygiene agents stay alcohol based except visibly soiled or spore and naked virus indications where soap's physical removal wins.
steps.say: Outbreaks rewrite the disinfectant shelf overnight; hands switch to soap when spores circulate.

left.title: Escalation triggers
points: Blood spills: high ppm chlorine after cleaning

right.title: Hand hygiene exceptions
points: Soap and water for spores and visible soil
